drafts.neutral_framing: Should Smith County publish its payments — who was paid, how much, and for what — as data anyone can download and search?
drafts.final_wording: Should Smith County publish every payment as open data anyone can download and search?
drafts.final_wording_note: Framed around publishing records the county already keeps, in a format that meets the Texas Comptroller’s transparency standard.
shaping_notes: A question about the county’s own disclosure format — not about any person, candidate, or ballot measure. Clears the bright lines.

Grounded in what was and was not found: the county posts budget books and its audit report is online (on a commissioner’s site), but no check register or open spending portal was found (Docket #7). Tarrant County posts a downloadable check register.

drafts.background: Smith County’s FY27 budget is $198 million. The budget books show how much each office is given. They do not show what was bought. No county check register or open spending portal was found in our search (Docket #7) — that means not found yet, not hidden. Some Texas counties post every payment as downloadable data, and the Texas Comptroller gives a Transparency Star for it.

drafts.neutral_framing: Should Tyler Water Utilities pilot a biological filter before treatment?
drafts.final_wording: Should Tyler Water Utilities run a pilot of a biological filter before treatment?
drafts.final_wording_note: Framed as a pilot the utility can run on its own, measured before and after — not a commitment to build.
shaping_notes: A question about how our shared water is treated — not about any person, candidate, or ballot measure. Clears the bright lines.
Grounded in the utility’s own water-quality report and in published measurements of living filters, with their limits stated on the water page.
drafts.tier_note: Open as a Tier 0 sentiment poll: no account, one voice per browser, changeable until close. Tier 0 is displayed but never cited as verified resident opinion — verification tiers arrive with the full voting layer.
drafts.background: Tyler’s 2025 water report lists trihalomethanes at a highest average of 58 ppb (limit 80 ppb), and organic carbon in its lake water as high as 8.81 mg/L. Organic matter is the raw material that chlorine byproducts form from. A biological filter is one method for reducing it before chlorine is added; results vary by site. The evidence and its limits are on the water page.

drafts.background: People held in the Smith County jail run a garden on Highway 155 and give the produce to the East Texas Food Bank (KETK, June 2023). The facts, the evidence, and the limits are on the From holding to building page.
